steps: Identify the data type (categorical, discrete, continuous, bivariate)
Choose the correct chart type for the data

For pie charts: use angle/360 × total to find frequency
method_card.title: Representing Data
method_card.content:
Bar charts: Bars represent frequencies. Heights are proportional. Use for categorical or discrete data.

Pie charts: Angle per category = \(\frac{\text{frequency}}{\text{total}} \times 360°\). To read: \(\frac{\text{angle}}{360} \times \text{total}\).

Scatter graphs: Plot bivariate data. Positive correlation: both increase. Negative correlation: one increases, the other decreases. No correlation: no pattern. The line of best fit (LOBF) passes through \((\bar{x}, \bar{y})\). Interpolation (within range) is reliable; extrapolation (outside range) is not.
method_card.example:
A pie chart represents 120 people. The 'Bus' sector is 90°. How many travel by bus?

\(\frac{90}{360} \times 120 = 30\) people

steps: Stacked bars: read each part, add them for the total, then one part as a percentage: part ÷ total × 100.
Comparing pie charts: convert each chart's sector to a frequency first, because equal angles on different totals mean different counts.
Line of best fit: substitute the x-value into its equation to estimate y. Inside the data range (interpolation) is reliable, outside (extrapolation) is not.
gold.title: Gold: composite charts and lines of best fit

example.question: A stacked bar shows North = 40, South = 30, East = 30. What percentage is North?

steps: Bar charts: follow the top of a bar across to the number axis. Each gridline is worth the scale shown, so a bar 5 gridlines up on a scale of 5 means 25.
Pie sectors: turn an angle into people with (angle ÷ 360) × total, and a frequency into an angle with (frequency ÷ total) × 360.
Correlation: both quantities rising together is positive; one rising as the other falls is negative; no pattern means none.
bronze.title: Bronze: reading charts and simple pie sectors

steps: Angle to frequency: divide the angle by 360 to get the fraction, then multiply by the total.
Frequency to angle: divide the frequency by the total, then multiply by 360. A missing sector = 360 minus the known angles.
Range: highest value minus lowest. Modal class: the group with the highest frequency.
